answer: We prove Sybil resistance by coupling dynamic collateral bonds with a falcon signature scheme and a yarrow-indexed zero-knowledge verifiable delay. For an adversary attempting identity multiplication across k nodes, subgame-perfect slashing matrices impose quadratic penalties that render expected attack utility strictly negative relative to holding the underlying relic asset. This capital barrier ensures single-identity strategies strictly dominate identity splitting, enforcing convergence to a unique strict Nash equilibrium.
